model: gpt-6.1-terra via signed-in local Codex CLI

methods.delivery: One fresh session per recording per condition. The only tool released two consecutive audio-only views and an end marker. Responses were captured from production play and Viewing.advance on the original channels. Both arms received the same spectrograms, measurements, AST estimates and CoNeTTE wide captions, with no raw WAV attachment, ASR or optional large waveform model. The changed arm also received the recent captions when available. No sound filenames, source metadata or keys were shown.
methods.reference_check: All 104 delivered turn captions were independently rerun through the original b1541d7 and new waveform workers. The old report equals the new one with the recent_windows field omitted. Three digitally silent second intervals had no local caption. The separate door test exercised the live MCP with speech checks.
methods.sources: ESC-50 fold 5, one preexisting recording for each of 50 distinct classes, sorted by SHA256(reel-listening-windows/v1/ + filename). Join two five-second native 44.1 kHz mono recordings, or use five seconds of zero samples as listed. Repeats use the same recording twice. Preserve PCM sample values. Readers could choose the supplied exact names, none of these, silence or unsure. Ground truth is the source label, not listeners re-rating the edits.
methods.original_events: Six contiguous seconds of original Perception Test audio, three on either side of an annotated onset. No waveform substitution. Candidate onsets at least one second long, with a different preceding source annotated for at least 0.4 seconds in the first three seconds and absent from the last three. No other named event overlaps the last three seconds for over 0.1 seconds. Use distinct recordings. Order candidate tuples by SHA256(reel-current-sound-013/ + Python str(tuple)), cover distinct target classes first, then allow up to two etc. The two listed alternatives are the earlier and current labels. An annotation identifies an event, not every sound possibly audible. No new human forced choices.
methods.urban: The 12 original MACS/TAU field recordings used in the earlier audio-cues/macs collection, unchanged. Two five-second views, stopping at each source end; one is shorter than ten seconds by one sample. The GPT question covers the whole recording. Each human annotated the whole recording. Set overlap is intersection over union, 1 for two empty lists. Average by recording. To reproduce the updated urban score use examples/check_soundscape_agreement.py on this JSON and the authors’ MACS.yaml with --macs.
methods.caption_rank: Separate automatic lexical/semantic check, without GPT: embed each local caption and “the sound of ” + each offered source using sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 revision 1110a243fdf4706b3f48f1d95db1a4f5529b4d41. Average the caption vectors across active native channels, choose highest dot product. No rejection option. Score only cases with an in-list answer.
methods.limits: One GPT response per condition per recording. Interval resampling measures across-recording variation. It does not measure rerun variability. Several synthetic cases reuse sound sources.

door.details: Live MCP with local ASR and no native audio attachment, old and new caption worker, anonymous clips. B has only room tone; A adds the key recording. See examples/make_door_trial.py.

before.A: A simple illustration of a closed brown door against a beige wall remains essentially unchanged throughout. The audio reader suggests jingling or rattling, possibly keys, with a louder burst near the end; the source is uncertain, and no intelligible words were detected.
before.B: A simple illustration of a closed brown door against a beige wall remained unchanged throughout. The audio reading suggests a steady fan-like sound, though its source is uncertain; no intelligible words were detected.

after.A: A simple illustration shows a closed brown door in a beige wall, with no obvious visual change. The audio reading suggests jingling or rattling, possibly keys, becoming louder briefly before fading; no intelligible words were detected.
after.B: A simple illustration shows a closed brown door against a pale wall, with no apparent visual change. The audio reading suggests a faint, steady fan-like sound, though its source is uncertain; no intelligible words were detected.
